metadata.note: The Ashuelot Railroad connected Keene, NH to the Vermont border, running down the Ashuelot River valley through Winchester and the village of Ashuelot to Hinsdale, then across to Brattleboro, VT via connecting trackage. It ran its first trains in December 1850, complementing the Cheshire Railroad's 1848 arrival in Keene from the other direction (see cheshire_railroad.geojson). Consolidated with the Connecticut River Railroad in 1890 and taken over by the Boston and Maine in 1893; the corridor helped power the late-19th-century mill boom along the Ashuelot River. Geometry is real-traced from OpenStreetMap (much of the route is now the Ashuelot Recreational Rail Trail, tagged as former railway); every hop resolved to a connected, plausible real track path with no straight-line fallbacks needed.

All hops resolved to connected, plausible paths.

metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
